description:
FILED s464a (Opus, 2026-09-02) while shipping #964 (the sub-frame leave rule),
which the s464 design explicitly scoped this OUT of: "perl copies at BOTH sub
and eval-BLOCK exit (pp_leavesub / pp_leaveeval) and NOT at `do { }` -- the
eval frame is a SIBLING rule, out of this task's scope: file it."

THE RULE.  perl's pp_leaveeval mortal-copies the value an `eval { }` or a
string `eval` block leaves with, exactly as pp_leavesub does for a sub; `do { }`
does NOT (it is not a frame -- `\do { $x }` IS `\$x`, probed).  PCL applies the
copy at the SUB frame only (%p-leavesub, reached through the p-sub-frame macro),
so an eval frame still hands the caller the variable's own box and every
aliasing consumer writes through it.

PROBE (scratch p964/evalframe.pl; perl 5.40.3 vs ./runpcl on the s464a branch,
which already has #964 shipped -- so these are the RESIDUE, not #964's rows):

    my $x = 1;
    for (eval { $x }) { $_ = 5 }            perl 1   PCL 5
    my $r = \eval { $x }; $$r = 6;          perl 1   PCL 6
    for (eval '$x') { $_ = 9 }              perl 1   PCL 9
    my @l = (1,2);
    for my $v (eval { @l }) { $v = 'W' }    perl "1 2"   PCL "W W"

  and the two that ALREADY agree, which are the boundary of the fix:
    for (do { $x }) { $_ = 7 }              perl 7   PCL 7   (do is not a frame)
    my $d = \do { $x }; $$d = 8;            perl 8   PCL 8
    sub s1 { my $y=2; for (eval { $y }) { $_=3 } $y }   perl 2   PCL 2
      -- this one agrees only because the SUB frame around it copies; the eval
         frame inside it is still wrong, it just cannot be observed there.

WHERE.  cl/pcl-runtime.lisp: `p-eval-block` (the `(catch :p-return â¦)` inside
its handler-case) and the string-eval `(catch :p-return â¦)` in p-eval-string's
`result` binding.  The MECHANISM is already written and tested -- %p-leavesub
and its two helpers, plus the p-sub-frame macro -- so the change is a second
frame macro (or the same one) at those two sites.  p-sort-cmp stays a bare
catch (its value is numified) and p-goto-sub stays one (the target's own frame
copies).

WHAT TO CHECK BEFORE ASSUMING IT IS ONE LINE.  #964 measured two traps at the
sub frame that this site will meet too:
  (1) THE VECTOR SHAPE IS SEMANTIC.  PCL distinguishes an ARRAY (adjustable,
      fill pointer) from a LIST TEMP (a simple vector whose aggregate elements
      are still unflattened).  #964's first version copied a list temp into an
      adjustable vector and every nested aggregate stopped being flattened --
      `sub steps { qw(x), $_[0]->SUPER::steps }` yielded ARRAY(0x1) and the
      whole gate's moo-01.t died.  %p-leavesub-vector preserves the shape; use
      it, do not re-derive it.
  (2) A GENUINE DUALVAR ($!, Scalar::Util::dualvar) carries its two halves on
      the BOX, so the plain-scalar arm must not unbox it (%pcl-dualvar-p /
      %p-dualvar-copy).  #964's first version lost the numeric half and
      Pl/t/errno-01.t's four dualvar rows failed.
  (3) `$@` handling: p-eval-block's prog1 sets $@ AFTER the body; the copy
      must sit inside the prog1's value position, not around the whole form.
  (4) Context: at the eval frame *wantarray* is the eval's own caller's, the
      same property %p-leavesub relies on -- verify, do not assume.

BAR (the #964 recipe): the four diverging rows above on both emission paths;
`do { }` and the two agreeing rows unmoved; a Pl/t guard beside
Pl/t/return-copy-01.t, inverse-verified on a base worktree; corpus-diff (the
change is runtime-only, so it will be IDENTICAL -- that is not a pass, it is
why the full sweep is mandatory); full perl-tests sweep + the companion legs
for a cl/ change; ir-spec Â§5.3's "Not frames" bullet updated (it names this
task).


=== SHIPPED s464aw (agent AW, round 22, 2026-09-02).  #987 CLOSED.

THE FIX IS TWO CALL SITES AND NOTHING ELSE.  `%p-leavesub' â #964's rule,
already written and tested â now wraps the `catch :p-return' at
`p-eval-block' and at the string eval's `result' binding.  No new rule, no new
helper, and the FOUR TRAPS this task listed cost nothing to clear because they
are properties of the mechanism, not of the site:

  (1) the semantic VECTOR SHAPE: %p-leavesub-vector already preserves it;
  (2) the DUALVAR arm: already there (probe row q7, `local $! = 2;
      my $d = eval { $! }' reads 2/str on both sides);
  (3) $@: the copy sits in the PROG1'S VALUE POSITION, so `box-set $@ ""'
      still runs after the body and the error path still yields a bare nil
      (probe row q4: `eval { die "boom\n"; 1 }' is undef with $@ = "boom\n");
  (4) CONTEXT: *wantarray* at the eval frame is the eval's caller's, verified
      rather than assumed by probe rows q2/q3 â `my $n = eval { @l3 }' is 3
      and `my @g = eval { @l3 }' is (1,2,3), unchanged.

THE 23-ROW PROBE FILE, perl 5.40.3 vs ./runpcl, EIGHT rows moved:
    for (eval { $x }) { $_ = 5 }            5 -> 1
    my $r = \eval { $x }; $$r = 6           6 -> 1
    for (eval '$x') { $_ = 9 }              9 -> 1
    my $r = \eval '$x'; $$r = 11           11 -> 1
    for my $v (eval { @l }) { $v = 'W' }  W W -> 1 2
    for my $v (eval '@l')  { $v = 'W' }   W W -> 3 4
    for my $v (eval { %h }) { $v = 'W' }    W -> 1
    sub w { $_[0]='A' } w(eval { $x })      A -> 1
and FIFTEEN held, which is the inverse guard: `do { }` foreach and backslash,
the eval's VALUE, its scalar and list context, the die path's $@, a blessed
return's `ref`, the $! dualvar, an empty list, undef, a nested eval, a nested
aggregate, an eval inside a sub, and map.  IDENTICAL under PCL_OPT=none.

`do { }` NEEDED NO EXCLUSION.  It is not a frame in perl (`\do { $x }' IS
`\$x', probed) and PCL's `do' has no `catch :p-return' of its own, so there was
nothing to hang a copy on and nothing does â the boundary held by
construction rather than by a guard in the code.

WHAT THE GUARD ROW FOR THAT BOUNDARY TURNED UP, AND IT IS NOT THIS TASK'S:
written with a plain `my $x', the `do' rows FAIL â and they fail on the BASE
too.  `do { $lexical }' does not alias in PCL for ANY lexical kind (file,
block or sub); only a package variable does.  The discriminator is that the
bare `for ($f) { $_ = 5 }' on the SAME file lexical DOES alias, so the
aliasing machinery works and it is the `do' lowering that drops the cell.
PRE-EXISTING, verified on an 80b715c worktree, the OPPOSITE direction from
#964/#987, and filed as task **#1008**.  The guard rows therefore use `our`,
with a comment saying exactly this â with `our` the aliasing works on the base,
so an over-eager copy at a non-frame still FAILS the row, which is what an
inverse guard is for.

BARS MET.  Gate 192/6540 (only the 13 pclxs xs rows; 6538 + the 2 new guard
rows).  Full sweep GATE clean, TOTAL passing 18347 (+0), drops 5 = census,
0 new / 0 fixed.  Companion op/ + comp/ (the dirs that carry eval.t, die.t and
the exception families).  Guard `Pl/t/return-copy-01.t' 6 -> 8 rows (group E,
beside #964's A-D), BOTH inverse-verified FAILING on an 80b715c worktree â
note row 8, the "boundary" row, is a mover too (`sub s1 { for (eval { $y })
{ $_=3 } $y }' over a FILE-level $y reads 3 on the base and 2 here).
RUNTIME-ONLY: no generation bump, no artifact regeneration, corpus cannot
move.  `docs/ir-spec.md` 5.3 gains the eval-frame and `do`-is-not-a-frame
bullets (its "Not frames" list named THIS task and now names `do { }`), and
6.3's eval steps say the value is copied.

COST: one `%p-leavesub` per eval exit â inline, raw arm first, so a raw value
(the common eval result) is one struct typep and one special read with no
call.  Not separately benched: it is the same inline rule #964 measured at
the far hotter sub-frame site, where every named bench row stayed inside the
control band, and an eval exit is orders of magnitude rarer than a sub return.


=== FABLE REVIEW + MERGE (s464, 2026-09-02) === diff read; probes vs perl 5.40.3 on both PCL_OPT paths (ovl.pl 37 rows for #972/#987: 33 identical, the 4 diffs are the declined #960(a) refusal); rebased and merged ff into main (round 22: AW 3d666ea, AX 300d47f); legs on the final tree in DECIDED s464 round-22 record.
subject: eval { } and string eval are FRAMES too: perl copies at eval exit (pp_leaveeval) and PCL returns the variable's box -- the sibling of #964, five probe rows
